name: Self
typeSystem: Dynamic, uniformly object-based with no classes at all: every value is an object, and new objects are created by cloning and modifying existing 'prototype' objects rather than instantiating a class.
runtime: Self pioneered polymorphic inline caches and adaptive, feedback-directed just-in-time compilation to make a pure, classless, message-send-everything language run fast. This research strongly influenced later adaptive virtual machines, with especially direct technical and personnel lineage into Java HotSpot and broader influence on engines such as V8.

runtimes.name: Self VM (adaptive JIT)
runtimes.role: Research virtual machine that pioneered polymorphic inline caches and adaptive recompilation, techniques later adopted by HotSpot Java and V8 JavaScript.

compilers.name: Self VM compiler
compilers.role: Just-in-time compiles message sends, using feedback from running code to specialise and re-optimise hot call sites.

concurrencyModel: The Self system provides processes managed by a preemptive round-robin scheduler. Process objects can be forked, suspended, resumed, or terminated, with semaphores, barriers, locks, and serialising channels available for coordination.

codeExample.caption: An object delegating to a prototype and overriding a method
codeExample.source:
| animal dog |
animal: (| speak = ('Hello!' printLine) |).
dog: (| parent* = animal. speak = ('Woof!' printLine) |).
dog speak.
